pr.title: Dismiss a pull request from its loops in the band
pr.head: c164895420baeaded13ffb773f26a051a2268184

summary: Projector's band is the strip above the Claude Code prompt that lists the pull requests a session's loops act on. A loop is a long-running agent workflow: the watch loop fixes review findings on pull requests, and the review loop reviews each new head. Each loop reads its scope from a tracked file, one owner/repo#number per line, which its watcher script reads again every cycle.

Until this change, the only way to stop a loop acting on one pull request was to edit its tracked file by hand. The review watcher and the band already honored a line !owner/repo#number, called an exclusion, that keeps a pull request out wherever it sits in the file. Nothing wrote that line, and the watch loop's watcher reported it as a malformed line.
This pull request does three things:

1. Two CLI commands. project loop drop owner/repo#number --tracked <file> appends an exclusion, and project loop restore removes it, so a dismissal can be undone.
  2. The watch loop honors exclusions. watch-threads.sh now parses ! lines the way watch-prs.sh already does.
  3. A dismiss button in the band. A pull request's drawer gains dismiss beside discuss. It runs project loop drop for each of the session's tracked files that lists the pull request, then reloads the band and says which loops stopped.
The pull request is the top layer of a stack on #298, which groups the band's pull requests by author. The review of this head found no blocking issue.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Tracked file: a loop's list of pull requests, one owner/repo#number a line.
  • Exclusion: a line !owner/repo#number that keeps that pull request out, matched without regard to letter case.
  • Watcher: the shell script a loop runs to poll GitHub, watch-prs.sh for the review loop and watch-threads.sh for the watch loop.
  • Drawer: the details a band line opens to when you press its number.

groups.title: The CLI writes and removes exclusions
groups.kicker: project loop drop and project loop restore edit a tracked file
intro: A new module, loop.py, owns the only code that changes a tracked file's exclusions, so the band and an agent edit the file the same way. Both commands check the reference against the same owner/repo#number pattern the inbox uses, exit 65 on a malformed reference, and exit 66 when the tracked file does not exist.

drop appends rather than rewriting the file, because a watcher or an agent may append a pull request to the same file at the same moment. It does nothing when the file already holds an exclusion for the pull request in any letter case. restore rewrites the file atomically without that pull request's exclusions and leaves its plain line alone, so the pull request returns to the loop.

files.note: New module: drop appends an exclusion, restore removes every exclusion for one pull request.

checks.text: is_exclusion trims the line, needs the ! directly before the reference, and ignores case. The review compared it with parseTracked in hooks/parse.ts and parse_tracked in both watchers: a line this counts as present is one every reader excludes.
When the file does not end in a newline, drop writes one first, so the exclusion starts a line of its own.
restore writes through write_through, which follows a symlink and keeps the file's mode; test_removes_only_the_pull_requests_exclusions_in_any_letter_case checks the mode, and the review ran it.

files.note: Registers the loop subcommand and prints dropped, restored, or unchanged, as text or with --json.

checks.text: Errors reach main, which maps ProjectorError to exit 65 and the new TrackedFileNotFound to 66.

files.note: Runs both commands against a temporary tracked file: case-insensitive matching, a missing trailing newline, refusals, and drop followed by restore.

groups.title: The watch loop honors exclusions
groups.kicker: watch-threads.sh parses ! lines as watch-prs.sh does
intro: The watch loop's watcher, watch-threads.sh, reported an exclusion as a malformed line. Its parse_tracked now collects exclusions and plain entries in one pass and prints only the entries no exclusion names. The two-pass shape matters because an exclusion can sit above the line it excludes.
The review loop's skill gains the same sentence as the watch loop's, so an agent running either loop writes and removes an exclusion through the CLI.

checks.text: The new parser follows the review watcher's parse_tracked in skills/start-review-loop/scripts/watch-prs.sh line for line, except that it keeps duplicate entries, as it did before.

files.note: parse_tracked skips each entry an exclusion names, matched case-insensitively. The header comment describes exclusions and is rewrapped.

checks.text: The match wraps each key in spaces, so acme/app#1 never matches an exclusion for acme/app#12.

files.note: Tells the watch loop's agent what an exclusion does and that project loop drop and restore write it.
Names project loop drop and restore beside the exclusion line it already described; the rest of the paragraph is rewrapped.
An exclusion above its entry, in another letter case, keeps that pull request out and stops every GitHub call for it.

groups.title: Dismiss in the band
groups.kicker: A pull request's drawer gains dismiss, which drops it from the session's loops
intro: Pressing dismiss in a pull request's drawer stops every loop of this session that tracks the pull request. dismissPr reads the session's tracked files again, runs project loop drop once for each file that still lists the pull request, closes the drawer, reloads the band so the line goes, and shows a toast such as stopped watching and reviewing acme/app#258. When the CLI refuses, the band shows the CLI's error and keeps the drawer open.
The drawer's actions now share one helper, drawActions, with an inbox item's drawer, so both draw plain buttons on one row with | between them.

checks.text: An inbox item's drawer already has a dismiss action, which marks the item done. On a pull request the same word means stop the session's loops acting on it.

files.note: Adds dismissPr, factors trackedSets out of load, makes closeDrawer take the whole drawer key, and adds the shared drawActions row.

checks.text: trackedSets keeps each loop's tracked path, which adopt already resolved through canonical, so project loop drop writes the same file the watcher reads. The review traced the path from adopt.
A refusal on the second file returns after the first file was already dropped; the finally block still toasts the loop that stopped and reloads, so the line stays only under the loop that refused.
All three callers of closeDrawer now pass a full drawer key: item:<ref> for an item, keyOf(pr) for a pull request. The review searched for every caller.

files.note: Dismiss drops the pull request from both loops, toasts once, and removes the line; a refusal toasts the CLI's error and keeps the line.
